about: Denning's corrections to the win-probability model. Kinds: direction (curve can only rise or fall: increasing true/false), drop (variable not used), main_drop (no curve of its own, its pairs stay), interaction (always offer this pair, written 'a & b'), no_interaction (never pair the term with the variables in 'with'), cap (effect limited to max_points), cap_test (the data picks a cap from 'options' or none, model.py cap_test). Each needs a reason. Every fit reports accuracy with and without them.

corrections.reason: Denning (agreeing with Claude's batch 3 finding): Lord damage only decides a match at 28:00 (the tiebreak); before that a team can deal a lot of Lord damage and still lose to a Lord kill, so Lord damage should be read together with the clock.

Denning (2026-11-07, agreeing with Claude's batch 7 finding): each team's Lord damage per second is fixed by its build, so it is one value per team per match; the curves zigzagged in mirror image, each step resting on 11 to 14 team-matches with no trend in win rate (memorizing which teams won). Held-out log loss on 91 matches: as before 0.404, both dropped 0.413, directions 0.393, cap at 5 points 0.377 (best), cap + directions 0.384.

Denning (2026-11-07, agreeing with Claude's batch 8 finding): healing monks are one value per team per match and almost every team runs 3 (0 monks: 1 team-match, 4 monks: 5), so the curves' extreme steps rest on almost nothing and zigzag in mirror image. Held-out log loss on 113 matches: as before 0.385, cap at 5 points 0.382, dropped 0.367 (best).

Denning (agreeing with Claude's batch 9 review, 133 matches): the Lord damage curve on its own acts as a sign marker, not the 28:00 tiebreak: +-7 to 9 points once any Lord damage exists, the most negative band reads +31.6 (backwards), and teams ahead on Lord damage won 88% with alive +0.94 and morale +78 (it marks who got into the pit). Only its pairing with the clock is kept.

Denning (agreeing with Claude's batch 9 review): Lord damage per second and the spike build are fixed by the build, one value per team per match; paired with morale they memorize which teams won (morale x Lord damage per second came back 3rd and 4th, 0.42 each, despite the batch 7 caps on the main terms).
Denning (agreeing with Claude's batch 9 review): as for morale_diff, build-fixed values are not paired with morale.

Denning (agreeing with Claude's batch 9 review): the curve steps 35 points at one player, but at the same morale (-20 to 20) teams won 64% / 50% / 37% across the same steps, a real gap of about 13; it overlaps death penalty and took part of morale's effect (worst miss: Fun v hold 2:00, hold given 0.4% and won, this variable -46). The data picks the cap, or none if no cap predicts unseen matches better.
Denning (agreeing with Claude's batch 9 review): more enemy time down can only help; the curve read backwards for 7 to 38 s, mirroring alive_diff. Direction forced rather than dropping the variable.
